pages.title: Well come to Steel Frame
pages.purpose: Introduce steel-frame, explaining the framework's purpose as a fault tolerant frontend kit and key differentiators (synchronous updates, strong typing, predectibility, developer experience)

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Quick start guide for creating a steel-frame application using npm create steel-frame, basic project structure, and first component

pages.title: Components and UI
pages.purpose: Cover component definition patterns, JSX syntax, elements attributtes and strong HTML standards used: class, not className, onclick, not onClick etc., the developer can paste any valid HTML to component and it will be accepted

pages.title: Defining Components
pages.purpose: Show how to define components using view(), component() for components, page() for file-based routing, and the differences between them

pages.title: JSX and Templates
pages.purpose: Explain JSX syntax, how attributes/events/bindings work, class and style handling (static vs dynamic)

pages.title: Built-in Components
pages.purpose: Document If/ElseIf/Else for conditional rendering, For for lists, Watch for reactive observation, Delay for deferred rendering, Slot for content projection

pages.title: Props and Slots
pages.purpose: Explain prop passing via input parameter, slot pattern for content projection, model vs slot props in Slot component, and callback pattern

pages.title: Lifecycle Hooks
pages.purpose: Document beforeMount() (sync), afterMount() (sync/async), beforeDestroy() hooks, and their use cases including safe() wrapping

pages.title: State Management
pages.purpose: Cover reactive variables and object properties with $ prefix, global stores, component models, reactive collections, computed values, and async data handling

pages.title: Reactive Variables
pages.purpose: Explain $-prefixed variables, ref() for explicit creating References, bind() for expressions, calculate() for computed functions, watch() for side effects

pages.title: Stores and Models
pages.purpose: Document store() for global persistent state, model() for component-scoped state with automatic clean up

pages.title: Reactive Collections
pages.purpose: Document arrayModel(), mapModel(), setModel() for reactive data structures, their are used automatically when the developer declare a const initialized with an Array, Map or Set value in a component

page_notes.content: Array model is not working corectly with pimitive values like booleans, numbers and strings

pages.title: Computed Values
pages.purpose: Explain bind() for reactive expressions (transforms expressions to track dependencies), calculate() for reactive functions, and that an reactive expression are created automatically when a constant is declared in component and its value contain reactive values (variable or object properties which name start with $)

pages.title: Async Data
pages.purpose: Document awaited() utility for handling promises in sync components, returning [error, data, retry] tuple for reactive loading state management

pages.title: Routing
pages.purpose: Cover router setup via src/pages folder presence and src/index.vasille.js as project entry point, screen/page components, navigation methods, loading states, and error/fallback handling

pages.title: Defining Routes and Screens
pages.purpose: Document route patterns (static /path, dynamic /(param)), screen() wrapper, ScreenProps interface with route parameters and query params

pages.title: Router Settings
pages.purpose: Explain usage of src/router/checkAccess.ts module as route access function, src/router/fallbackScreen.tsx module for handling of unexisting and restricted routes, src/router/errorScreen.tsx for error screen when the navigation is accepted but fails, src/router/loadingScreen.tsx for a loading screen showed before first page render, src/router/loadingOverlay.tsx for a overlay between pages on navigation

pages.title: Navigation Methods
pages.purpose: Document goTo() (full-page loading), ajax() (overlay loading), load() (silent preload), reload(), and NavigationMode enum

pages.title: Loading States
pages.purpose: Explain loadingScreen (full-page), loadingOverlay (AJAX-style), $currentUrl and $loadingUrl reactive references

pages.title: Modals and Prompts
pages.purpose: Document modal() HOF for creating modal components, prompt() for Promise-based user interaction, Portal abstraction, and timeout handling

pages.title: Styling
pages.purpose: Document styleSheet() for scoped CSS, theme() and dark() utilities for theming, mobile()/tablet()/laptop() for responsive design, and dynamic class generation

pages.title: Style Sheets
pages.purpose: Explain styleSheet() function, array-based media query syntax, dynamic class name generation, and CSSStyleSheet insertion mechanism

pages.title: Theming and Dark Mode
pages.purpose: Document dark() utility for theme-aware styles, body.dark class pattern, dual-rendering technique for theme transitions, and theme switching implementation

pages.title: Responsive Design
pages.purpose: Document mobile(), tablet(), laptop() utilities, breakpoint configuration via setMobileMaxWidth/setTabletMaxWidth/setLaptopMaxWidth, and media query generation

pages.title: Package Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the modular architecture with steel-frame as a facade over vasille-* packages (vasille, vasille-jsx, vasille-web, vasille-router, vasille-css, vasille-context, vasille-ssg)

pages.title: Core Concepts
pages.purpose: Introduce fundamental concepts: reactive system (IValue, Reference, Expression), component model (compose, view), and the synchronous update guarantee

pages.title: Reactive System
pages.purpose: Explain IValue interface, Reference (mutable state), Expression (computed values), and the on/off event system for reactive propagation

pages.title: Component Model
pages.purpose: Explain compose(), view(), component(), screen(), page() functions, Fragment context, and the component-as-function paradigm

pages.title: Synchronous Updates
pages.purpose: Explain the synchronous DOM update guarantee ('when the line of code is executed, the DOM and reactive things are already synced') and how it differs from async frameworks
